tasks.short: Stand watch while the vessel is under way

steps.what: Stand watches during specified periods while vessels are under way

tasks.design: The officer maintains the watch and uses existing navigation instruments {OTHER}. Electronic recordkeeping does not replace lookout, situational awareness or the specified watch period.
tasks.previous_blocker: Watchkeeping requires continuous attention to the vessel's surroundings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instruments support awareness without proving that watch time can be removed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising changing hazards and conflicting indications.
tasks.human_edge: The officer interprets the scene and takes responsibility for escalation.
tasks.altitude: Watch responsibility and presence remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: watchkeeping remains human; electronic-log capability does not establish reduced navigational watch time.

assumptions: Boundary is standing the watch, excluding separate log entry and manoeuvring tasks.
The responsible watch planner supplies the assignment and existing instruments supply navigation readings; the officer observes surroundings during s1. No structured all-clear signal is assumed.
OTHER means vessel navigation instruments. Use existing native displays first; runtime earns no human saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new watchkeeping system is introduced.
research_questions: Which watch observations are absent from existing instrument data?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. The full watch remains; logging savings are not applied to watch presence.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect vessels and equipment for safe operation

steps.what: Inspect vessels and equipment for efficient, safe operation and regulatory conformance

tasks.design: The officer inspects physical conditions against the current requirements in {DOCS}. No electronic status is treated as automatic proof of safe operation or conformance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deficiencies may require direct observation and contextual interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inspection guidance supports the task without removing the physical inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising hidden or conflicting signs of equipment problems.
tasks.human_edge: The officer knows when an apparently acceptable condition requires further investigation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: vessel inspection remains physical and judgement-led; the digest contains logbook capability rather than automated inspection evidence.

assumptions: Boundary is vessel and equipment inspection, excluding repairs and separately specified gauge-level checks in task 23811. Overlapping observations are assigned once.
The responsible vessel compliance owner supplies existing inspection requirements. The officer obtains condition observations during s1; no structured compliant-vessel flag is assumed.
Test native document access first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new inspection tool or reporting demand is introduced.
unknowns: Vessel-specific inspection scope and national or flag requirements
research_questions: Which deficiencies need direct observation beyond existing records?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Inspection and interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check hydraulic fluid, air pressure and oxygen gauges

steps.what: Read gauges to verify sufficient hydraulic fluid, air pressure or oxygen levels

tasks.design: The officer reads the installed gauges and checks adequacy against equipment requirements. Existing manuals in {DOCS} support the check without assuming remote sensor coverage or eliminating physical verification.
tasks.previous_blocker: A gauge reading needs equipment context and confidence that the indication is valid.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing gauges already provide readings; their runtime is not a new automation opportunity.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a misleading indication or a level unsuitable for current conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The officer interprets the indication in its physical setting.

reach.task: Clarify equipment-level requirements and abnormal indications
reach.learn: Gauge limitations and equipment operating conditions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing gauge runtime is not human labour; this design retains reading and adequacy checks.

assumptions: Boundary is the named level checks, excluding replenishment, repair and general inspection in task 23810.
Installed gauges produce readings and the responsible equipment owner supplies current requirements. The officer checks applicability during s1; no free structured sufficient-level label is assumed.
Use existing native indications first; no new sensor installation is presumed. Zero incremental upkeep because the process is unchanged.
research_questions: Which gauge checks require direct physical access even with existing remote displays?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. No saving from existing gauge runtime or uninstalled sensors.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Establish facts and applicable reporting requirements for suspected pilotage violations
Draft the pilotage violation report from verified incident facts

loop.input: Officer-selected incident facts, source references and required report structure
loop.output: Draft narrative with sourced facts and explicit unknowns
loop.check: Officer checks chronology, attribution, qualifications and that suspected conduct is not presented as a proven legal conclusion
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported passages are removed or written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native form fields handle fixed facts; varied incident narrative needs contextual wording

steps.what: Check and report suspected pilotage violations to the appropriate authority

tasks.design: Use existing incident templates in {DOCS} first, then a bounded loop for factual narrative from the officer's verified brief. The officer checks the exact report and submits it through the authorised {EMAIL} or {GOV_PORTAL} channel; the model makes no legal determination.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified incident facts must be expressed clearly for the authority.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can assist wording without deciding whether a law was violated.
tasks.still_hard: Separating observations from inference and identifying the applicable reporting route.
tasks.human_edge: The officer understands the incident and takes responsibility for accurate reporting.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in narrative drafting with factual and reporting responsibility retained.

reach.task: Clarify the evidence needed for an incident report
reach.learn: Evidence provenance and authority reporting requirements

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound incident drafting may reduce wording work, but no pilotage-reporting case establishes the proposed saving.

assumptions: Boundary is reporting observed suspected conduct, excluding authority investigation and legal determination. The US-specific task wording is adapted to applicable national, local and flag requirements without asserting a particular rule.

In s1 the officer captures incident time, location, vessel identities, observed conduct, source versions, witness attribution, unknown facts, required fields and authority destination; the full 40% remains. No free structured violation flag or incident brief is assumed.

Missing facts or unclear requirements return to manual investigation and writing; the draft cannot invent witnesses or legal conclusions. Test native incident forms first; existing runtime earns no saving.
Five extra focal hours count template changes, report audits and failed-draft handling; no additional authority or witness labour is transferred.
unknowns: Applicable reporting requirements and authorised sender
research_questions: Does drafting save time after chronology, attribution and legal-language checks?

already_counted.description: Incident verification and structured brief capture

incremental.description: Template maintenance, report audits and failed drafts

approvals.approved_version: Exact incident report, factual source versions, qualifications, attachments and authority recipient checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+30*0.70+30=91; gross 9%, net 4% after 5 focal upkeep. Range covers failed drafts with zero gain through 7 points of wording removed minus 5 upkeep. Fact finding, review and submission remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Watchkeeping and physical checks stay human; bounded incident wording offers a small conditional saving.
reach: Coordinate clear observations and evidence with engineers and inspectors.
role.ambitious_version: Traceable reporting without treating logbook capability as automated vessel command.
